accuracy.reason: All nine objectives accurately distinguish copying from partitioning, initial-copy/log handoff, asynchronous/synchronous acknowledgement stages, lag/read routing, write topologies, fenced failover and historical recovery. Primary RDS/PostgreSQL/MySQL/Cassandra and Brewer passages were inspected live.

evidence.quote: Synchronous replication does not necessarily wait for every replica. Nor does every synchronous mode guarantee that replica reads already show the change.

mechanisms.reason: Actors and state transitions are explicit: snapshot plus ordered log, receive versus apply, wait versus early success, authority/progress-based read routing, topology-dependent reconciliation, fencing/promotion/routing and backup/log replay. Cards 1-9 support tracing both normal propagation and failure.

evidence.quote: The initial copy and starting log position must agree.

coherence.reason: All nine card objectives follow their prerequisite order from copies to propagation and acknowledgements before lag, topology and failover. Diagrams at zero-based 1,4,6 reinforce copy/receive/apply, confirmed-but-unapplied data and one safe fenced promotion order without claiming a universal implementation.

evidence.quote: A missing response does not prove the old leader stopped.

decisions.reason: Weighs read capacity against write limits, remote waits against loss risk, authoritative reads against load, progress waits against delay, topology conflicts and historical recovery. Final policy is conditional on loss/freshness/latency/downtime and measured failure behavior, not an arbitrary replica count.

evidence.quote: Choose acceptable acknowledged-write loss, read freshness, write latency and recovery time before choosing replica settings.

clarity.reason: Snapshot, log, acknowledgement stages, lag, leader arrangements, split brain, fencing and point-in-time recovery are introduced at use. Concrete profile/deletion examples support transfer. Shared renderer/CSS inspected once; diagram captions match surrounding boundaries; no browser execution claimed.

evidence.quote: A fixed sleep or low average lag is not proof that a particular write is visible.

outcomes.reason: All six criteria supported across stack: replicated versus sharded groups, eligible read/takeover and routing, storage/coordination/write limits (costs explicit in policy answer), consistent initial snapshot with matching ordered stream, handoff correctness and received versus applied/read-visible state.

All seven criteria supported: configured success condition; async no remote wait and lag/loss trace; sync required set/count/stage; memory receipt versus durable versus visible apply; unavailable confirmations stall writes; limited failures and no all-replica freshness or logical-error protection.

All eight criteria supported: lag stage, read-own-completed-or-newer behavior, primary authority/load and selected-replica progress wait, stale-permitted reads and sleep/failover limits; single leader orders, multi-leader conflicts and timestamp loss, leaderless coordinator/reply/repair, no topology-only consistency guarantee.

All seven criteria supported: failover/promotion/split brain and network silence; suitable progress-aware candidate with async loss risk; old-writer fencing plus redirect/reconnect responsibilities; replicated accidental changes; retained historical backup/logs; real restore usability/time test. A concrete eligibility algorithm is not required by the criterion.

All four criteria supported: clarify loss/freshness/latency/downtime and failure scope; monitored reports on replicas, configured durable waits with cost and freshness routing; eligible fenced takeover and tested backups/restores with progress/health/wait measurements; storage/network/operations and no zero-loss/continuous-write guarantee from topology alone.

sourceChecks.claim: Inspected RDS read-replica copy, primary read/write versus read-only replica and separate creation/promotion/routing. Read offload is supported; copying data is distinct from dividing ownership and does not itself add primary write capacity.

Inspected PostgreSQL logical-replication initial snapshot, ongoing same-order changes and logical-versus-physical distinctions. Matching stream position preserves the copy handoff; MySQL receiver/applier followup confirms receipt and application are distinct.
Inspected PostgreSQL warm-standby asynchronous default and catastrophic-primary-loss window. Early acknowledgement avoids standby wait but does not establish another surviving copy.

Inspected exact warm-standby synchronous section: configured names/count, remote_write versus durable/on versus remote_apply and blocking without enough candidates. Stage-specific protection and latency/availability limits are supported.

Inspected MySQL WAIT_FOR_EXECUTED_GTID_SET: waits until specified transactions are applied, returns timeout/failure separately. Together with primary/replica rules this supports specific-progress freshness rather than average lag or fixed sleep.

Inspected Cassandra Dynamo coordinator sends writes to replicas and waits for configured response counts, timestamp conflict resolution and repair/reconciliation. PostgreSQL source/standby and logical-replication conflict passages support leader alternatives without universal topology guarantees.

Inspected PostgreSQL failover old-primary restart/fencing warning, promotion/routing requirements and lack of built-in failure detector. Silence cannot prove death; exclusive authority is a separate safety requirement.

Inspected PostgreSQL continuous archiving base backup plus retained WAL, historical stop points and replay-time costs. A current replica can propagate unwanted writes; retained history and tested usable restoration are distinct.

Inspected Brewer primary CAP retrospective on partition detection, operation restrictions, invariant choices and recovery/reconciliation. Agreement with unreachable copies limits availability; independent operations require explicit stale/conflict handling. This supports requirement-led policy rather than a topology guarantee.
